evidence.quote:
Offline LLM-based Feature Selection. Leveraging LLMs’ reasoning abilities, we introduce a
feature selection method using LLM-generated feature importance scores to identify the top-k most
important time-series-wise and text-wise features.

Features mentioned more frequently—either explicitly or implicitly—in annotations are assigned
higher importance scores.

reconciliation.reason: Lines 474-560 describe prompted domain-term extraction and annotation rewriting, followed by reviewer feedback that changes both extraction and annotation. This task-specific consistency check is execution control within an episode, not demonstrated evolution of reusable assets.

notes: Annotation is the primary output; forecasting and imputation are downstream evaluations through the inherited Time-MMD framework, not newly contributed forecasting/imputation modules. The OLMo ablation controls pretraining-data contamination but reports no chronological split, information cutoff, or temporal leakage check; on reassessment this is insufficient for R10 temporal validity. Human preferences concern informativeness, not measured action utility. Standard STL/FFT components are counted only within the contributed numerical toolbox integration. Textual-feature preparation and offline scoring are separated because their outputs also support the independently trained incremental selector; domain terminology extraction, rewriting and review remain one coupled annotation-refinement loop.
